hook_variants.template: ChatGPT isn't wrong sometimes. It can't tell the difference.
Why does ChatGPT sound so sure and still get things wrong?

sections.text: Every word is a guess. Confidence is just how likely that guess felt.
It finds patterns that sound like facts. It never checks if they are true.
sections.title: what it has vs what it lacks

sections.text: When it makes something up and sounds sure, that's a hallucination.
sections.title: hallucination
sections.body: made up, but said with confidence

sections.text: It never checks. It just picks the most likely next word and moves on.
Even the best models do this. Confidence never drops.
sections.title: Confidence vs fact-checking
sections.label: no fact-check pass

sections.text: So double-check before you trust. Follow for more on how AI works.

facts.claim: Hallucination = plausible but fabricated output, delivered confidently
facts.source_name: Survey on Hallucination in LLMs (Huang et al., 2023)

facts.claim: Cause: autoregressive next-token generation has no mechanism to verify against ground truth
Instruction tuning and retrieval (RAG) reduce but do not eliminate hallucinations
Hallucination rate varies by task; open-answer generation is the most error-prone
